questions.q: Run-time polymorphism in C++ is achieved by using
questions.e: A call through a base class pointer or reference to a virtual function is resolved at run time using the object's actual type. The other three are resolved at compile time.

questions.q: Which of the following is true about a constructor in C++?
o: It has the same name as its class and no return type
questions.e: A constructor is named after its class and has no return type, not even void. Constructors cannot be virtual or static.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true of a friend function of a class?
o: It is not a member of the class
It can access the private and protected members of the class
It is declared inside the class using the `friend` keyword
It is inherited by the classes derived from that class
questions.e: Friendship is not inherited: a friend of a base class does not automatically become a friend of its derived classes. The other three statements are true.

questions.q: Which keyword is used in C++ to raise an exception?
questions.e: `throw` raises an exception. `try` marks the guarded block and `catch` handles it. C++ has no `raise` keyword.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about C++.
I. A class having at least one pure virtual function cannot be instantiated.
II. A derived class that does not override an inherited pure virtual function becomes a concrete class.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: A class with a pure virtual function is abstract and no object of it can be created. A derived class that fails to override that function remains abstract too.

questions.q: Which of the following operators cannot be overloaded in C++?
questions.e: The scope resolution operator ::, along with ., .*, ?: and sizeof, cannot be overloaded. Operators such as +, [] and () can.

questions.q:
Regarding references in C++, consider the following.
I. A reference declared inside a function can be left uninitialised and bound later.
II. Once initialised, a reference can be made to refer to a different variable by assignment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are false. A reference must be initialised at its declaration and stays bound to that object for its whole life. Assigning to it changes the value of the referred object, not the binding.
